entries.026842bf02c0eaa1: Based on a joint venture plan with the U.S. company BorgWarner, the company established Aisin Warner Co., Ltd. It changed its name to AISIN AW CO., LTD. in March 1988, and absorbed Aisin AW Precision Co., Ltd. (established in March 1992) in June 2002 and Aisin AI Co., Ltd. (created in July 1991 through the separation and independence of the Shiroyama plant) in April 2019, respectively.

entries.1d876d2875070c3f: On order results, the securities report explains that all segments receive advance ordering instructions of around 3 months from major automakers including TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION and draw up production plans taking production capacity into account. The main customers are TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION and its group companies, and revenue is recorded from them in all reportable segments; that revenue in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥3,112,449 million (¥2,870,025 million in the previous year). Sales to TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION alone, 1 company, were ¥1,511,263 million, or 29.5% of total sales. By region, revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026, based on customer location, was ¥2,316,889 million in Japan, ¥941,282 million in the United States, ¥588,382 million in China and ¥1,271,209 million in other.
entries.25af315fe9111a8d: The main products are powertrain-related products that transmit the power of engines and motors to the wheels (automatic transmissions, hybrid transmissions, eAxle, and others), and driving safety-related products that stop the vehicle (disc brakes, electric parking brakes, and others). In addition, there are body-related products such as doors and sunroofs, LBS-related and other products such as car navigation systems, and aftermarket-related products that are repair and maintenance products. Products not installed in vehicles include energy solutions-related products such as gas heat pump air conditioners (GHP) and cogeneration systems, and femtosecond fiber lasers. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, external revenue from "Energy solutions-related and other" was ¥126,260 million. The company lists "combining its hardware strengths, such as powertrain units and brakes, with sensing and software" as a key initiative in its 2028 medium-term management plan.

entries.3ddbcd2f06690a24: The Prime Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange and the Premier Market of the Nagoya Stock Exchange, where it is currently listed, are continuations of these two lines. Manufacturing Co., Ltd. in July 1988, which then led to Aisin World Corporation of America, Inc. in October 1992 and to the establishment of Aisin Holdings of America, Inc., the North American holding company, in January 2001. entries.40e25295f0b29513: In May 1970, the company listed on the First Section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (now the Prime Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange) and the First Section of the Osaka Securities Exchange (delisted from the Osaka Securities Exchange First Section in December 2009), and in October of that year it established Aisin U.S.A. Co., Ltd. in the United States. On the Nagoya Stock Exchange, the company made its initial listing in July 1952, and in October 1961 it listed on the First Section of the same exchange (now the Premier Market of the Nagoya Stock Exchange).
entries.4262e3da8e051b7e: The current company name and present form begin here. With the development and production of transmissions, which had been carried out by a separate company, brought into the parent, powertrain-related operations became the company’s own business. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue was ¥5,117,764 million and profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥171,697 million, and the group consists of the company and 200 subsidiaries and affiliates (138 manufacturing companies, 19 sales companies and 43 others).

entries.53080d036af149af: It consists of AISIN CORPORATION and 200 subsidiaries and affiliates (138 manufacturing companies, 19 sales companies and 43 others). The breakdown of the number of companies directly expresses their roles, and it is a group with an overwhelming number of manufacturing companies. AISIN CORPORATION has regional headquarters heads who oversee each region and is responsible for formulating comprehensive strategies for their regions, among other things. The number of employees is 113,292 (plus an average of 23,417 temporary employees). The head office is in Kariya, Aichi, and [[company:toyota|TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION]] is the largest shareholder, holding 22.34% of issued shares (excluding treasury shares).

AISIN Automotive Ltda. in Brazil and others make and sell automotive parts. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥39,461 million, segment profit was ¥4,244 million and the number of employees was 819.
entries.6a7d2ce8bc105614: A company that makes automotive parts such as automatic transmissions and brakes and supplies them to automakers worldwide, centered on the [[company:toyota|Toyota Motor]] group.
entries.6dc77abf0b0f4daf: As Aichi Kogyo Co., Ltd., the company began manufacturing automatic transmissions. In June 1953, it had also begun manufacturing die-cast products; this was a period when the range of products expanded from castings and die-casting to transmissions.
entries.7d9fa171e0d380c1: It makes and sells automotive parts and energy solution-related equipment such as gas heat pump air conditioners, and earns revenue from them. Automotive parts are not products displayed in stores but parts delivered to automakers' factories, so the way orders are received is distinctive. The [[term:annual-securities-report|Annual Securities Report]] states: "All of the Group's [[term:segment|segments]] receive advance ordering instructions of around 3 months from major automakers including TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION, draw up production plans taking production capacity into account, and carry out production." This means it is a business in which the customers and quantities are foreseen before manufacturing. Its sales are heavily concentrated in the Toyota Group. Of the ¥4,991,503 million in revenue from external customers of the Automotive Parts Business in the fiscal year ended March 2026, ¥3,567,956 million was to the Toyota Group and ¥1,423,546 million to "OEM and other"; sales to [[company:toyota|TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION]] alone, 1 company, were ¥1,511,263 million, or 29.5% of total sales. All 5 reportable segments are regional (Japan, North America, Europe, China, ASEAN and India), and the idea of making and selling near automakers around the world is directly reflected in the shape of the organization.
entries.85449bfd5d50324c: Regarding orders received, the Annual Securities Report explains that all segments receive advance order instructions about three months ahead from major automakers including TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION, and draw up production plans taking production capacity into account.
entries.8c8f4bbb5c9628a3: This is the starting point that led to the company’s current main products. Automatic transmissions are at the core of the powertrain-related category (automatic transmissions, manual transmissions, continuously variable transmissions, hybrid transmissions, eAxles, etc.). For the fiscal year ended March 2026, increased unit sales of hybrid transmissions and eAxles were cited as the reason for higher revenue in the Japan segment, while a decline in unit sales of automatic transmissions was the reason for lower revenue in Europe and China.
entries.8f5cc5bbbc50ce77: Established Advics through joint investment with DENSO CORPORATION, Sumitomo Electric Industries, Ltd. and TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION
entries.9245997feb784062: The company absorbed Shinkawa Kogyo Co., Ltd., with capital of ¥656 million, through a merger, and changed its name from Aichi Kogyo Co., Ltd. to AISIN SEIKI CO., LTD. (capital of ¥2,856 million). Through this merger, it took over the Shinkawa plant (completed in March 1945) and the Shinho plant (completed in August 1961). Shinkawa Kogyo was also the company that, in March 1960, separated its casting division to form Takaoka Kogyo Co., Ltd. (now AISIN TAKAOKA CO., LTD.).

Kariya has been the company’s base since 1944, and the head office is still located at 2-chome, 1-banchi, Asahi-cho, Kariya City, Aichi Prefecture (the Kariya plant itself, completed in 1944, was transferred to Advics Co., Ltd. in April 2010).

Manufacturing, Inc. (Indiana), Aisin Drivetrain, Inc., Aisin Texas Corporation, Aisin North Carolina Corporation, and Aisin Automotive Guanajuato, S.A. de C.V. (Mexico) manufacture automotive parts. entries.c2dc3e40a3a469d2: This was a move in which several companies in the Toyota Group consolidated their brake businesses into one company. Advics remains a consolidated subsidiary in which AISIN CORPORATION holds 51.1% of voting rights (Kariya City, Aichi Prefecture; capital of ¥12,209 million), and overseas manufacturers in its group include Advics Manufacturing Ohio Co., Ltd. in the United States, Advics Manufacturing Mexico Co., Ltd. in Mexico, and Advics (Tianjin) Automotive Parts Co., Ltd. in China. entries.c41ab1d226f0b856: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥228,796 million, up 12.7% from the previous year. The company explains this as the result of investment in people and the future and corporate structure improvement efforts and structural reform effects, although there were impacts from tariffs. Profit before tax rose 43.0% to ¥247,941 million, due to a decrease in foreign exchange losses, and profit attributable to owners of the parent rose 59.6% to ¥171,697 million. The ratio of operating profit to revenue (operating margin) was 4.5%. By segment profit, Japan was ¥80,257 million, ASEAN and India ¥69,618 million, North America ¥39,133 million, China ¥30,657 million, Europe ¥4,123 million, and other ¥4,244 million; this ordering differs from the ranking by revenue, with ASEAN and India earning the second-highest profit after Japan.
entries.c564f29076d48940: Disc brakes and electric parking brakes
entries.c64592785392b23c: This was a move to strengthen the Japan segment by bringing domestic automotive parts companies into the group. AISIN SHIROKI CO., LTD. is a specified subsidiary based in Toyokawa City, Aichi Prefecture, with capital of ¥7,460 million and 100.0% voting rights held, and Art Metal Industry Co., Ltd. is a consolidated subsidiary based in Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture, with capital of ¥2,397 million and 80.3% voting rights held; both still manufacture automotive parts.
entries.c7f16d0c6339c35d: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥228,796 million, up 12.7% from the previous year.
entries.c888402d42bcbf9d: Operations in Japan. AISIN CORPORATION and subsidiaries such as ADVICS CO., LTD., Aisin Takaoka Co., Ltd., Aisin Shiroki Co., Ltd., Aisin Kiko Co., Ltd. and Aisin Kyushu Co., Ltd. manufacture and sell automotive parts and energy solution-related equipment. Because parts made in Japan are also shipped to overseas affiliated companies, in the fiscal year ended March 2026 there were inter-segment internal revenues of ¥696,682 million against revenue from external customers of ¥2,518,054 million. Segment profit was ¥80,257 million and the number of employees was 63,954, making it the largest region among the 5 reportable segments. The company explains that revenue increased owing to higher sales volumes of hybrid transmissions and eAxles, and that profit increased owing to the results of efforts to improve the corporate structure, despite investment in people and the future. The group's major customer overall is [[company:toyota|Toyota Motor]] Corporation and its group companies, which record revenue in all reportable segments; their revenue in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥3,112,449 million.

entries.e4c77d45df0a1aa7: Because this reorganization falls at the beginning of the fiscal year ended March 2026 (April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026), the figures for this year already reflect the post-merger structure. Following the 2021 merger with Aisin AW, this shows a continuing trend of bringing group companies into the parent company.

entries.f3c2a799caebec77: Tokai Hikoki Co., Ltd. was established with capital of ¥50 million through joint investment by Toyota Jidosha Kogyo Co., Ltd. (now [[company:toyota|TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION]]) and Kawasaki Kokuki Co., Ltd. (now Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Ltd.). The Kariya plant was completed in March 1944, and until the end of the war it manufactured aircraft engine parts. At the end of 1945 it switched to making sewing machines and automotive parts, and in December of that year it changed its name to Aichi Kogyo Co., Ltd.; in June 1949 it was reorganized as the new Aichi Kogyo Co., Ltd., with capital of ¥15 million, after receiving approval for a reconstruction plan under the Corporate Reconstruction Act. The securities report prints June 1949 as the “establishment” date.
entries.f5d1794652b6174f: The business in Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines, India and other countries. AISIN Powertrain (Thailand) Co., Ltd., AISIN Thai Automotive Casting Co., Ltd., AISIN Indonesia Automotive Co., Ltd., AT Indonesia Co., Ltd., Toyota AISIN Philippines, Inc., AISIN Automotive Haryana Private Limited (India) and others make and sell automotive parts. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥544,258 million, segment profit was ¥69,618 million, the second largest after Japan, and the number of employees was 17,599. The company explains that revenue and profit increased because of higher vehicle production volume at customers and higher sales volume of powertrain units, in addition to the continued trend of a weaker yen.
entries.f6a3a9a7f9ee83b7: The business in the People's Republic of China. Overseen by AISIN (China) Investment Co., Ltd. (Shanghai), Tianjin AISIN Automatic Transmission Co., Ltd., GAC AISIN Automatic Transmission Co., Ltd. (Guangzhou), Zhejiang Geely AISIN Automatic Transmission Co., Ltd. (Ningbo), AISIN Tangshan Gear Co., Ltd., AISIN Suzhou Automotive Parts Co., Ltd. and others make and sell automotive parts. GAC AISIN and Zhejiang Geely AISIN are automatic transmission companies formed as joint ventures with local automakers. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥566,074 million, segment profit was ¥30,657 million and the number of employees was 13,020. The company explains that revenue decreased because of lower sales volume of automatic transmissions, and that profit decreased also because of one-time costs such as structural reform expenses.
